scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

F-01.statement: PSP capture attempts show 242 duplicate orders with gateway timeout retries missing idempotency keys (Sep 9-10).

F-02.statement: On 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10, orders_with_2_captures equals gateway_timeout_retries (118 and 124), showing duplicate captures associated with timeout retries.

F-03.statement: Gateway idempotency_key_enforcement setting turned off by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 (temporary latency debugging, no rollback).

F-04.statement: Weekly duplicate charge ticket counts show a sharp increase in weeks 2026-W37 and W38.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-DUPLICATE-CHARGES.statement: Customers are experiencing duplicate charges due to a system bug causing double capture attempts.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: Payment gateway idempotency‑key enforcement is disabled, allowing retries to create duplicate captures.

H-DUPLICATE-CAPTURE-REQUESTS.statement: The checkout process erroneously sends duplicate capture requests to the PSP (handoff H‑CAPTURE).

H-PSP-RETRY-GLITCH.statement: The PSP incorrectly processes network retries, generating duplicate successful capture acknowledgments that prompt the shop to retry.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The PSP logs show 242 duplicate orders in Sep 9-10 where every second capture was a gateway timeout retry lacking an idempotency key, indicating duplicate charges stem from missing idempotency on shop-side retries; earlier period shows no duplicate orders despite many timeout retries that were deduplicated by the PSP and sent with idempotency keys.

The observation shows that on Sep 9-10, orders with two captures equal the number of gateway timeout retries, indicating duplicate captures arise when retries lack idempotency. Earlier days with many timeout retries had zero duplicate captures, showing the PSP deduplicates retries when idempotency keys are present.

The configuration audit shows that payment gateway idempotency-key enforcement was disabled on 2026-09-09 by SH-PAY for latency debugging and has not been rolled back, meaning retries lack deduplication.
The weekly ticket counts show a low baseline of duplicate charge tickets in weeks 35-36, then a sharp rise to 288-301 tickets in weeks 37-38, indicating a recent surge in duplicate charge incidents.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports that idempotency‑key enforcement on the payment gateway was turned off on 09‑09 for latency debugging and has not been rolled back, leaving retries without deduplication. This configuration change explains why gateway timeout retries can produce duplicate captures.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder confirms that customers are upset about double charges and desire faster, nicer apology replies, indicating the symptom is real and a need for improved communication.

proposal.root_problem: Disabled idempotency-key enforcement on the payment gateway causes gateway timeout retries to lack deduplication, resulting in duplicate charges.
causal_chain: Gateway timeout retries continue at baseline rate.
Retries lack idempotency keys because enforcement is disabled.
PSP does not deduplicate retries missing idempotency key.
Second capture creates a duplicate charge.
Customers observe duplicate charge and file support tickets (E-04).

assumptions.statement: No other system changes occurred between Sep 1-8 and Sep 9-10 that could affect duplicate charge rates.

unknowns.resolution_path: Observe weekly duplicate charge ticket count after toggling gateway-config.set_capture_idempotency to 'on' and confirming with payments operations.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Continue existing duplicate charge monitoring and alerting while the configuration remains off.

success_criteria.statement: Weekly duplicate charge ticket count returns to baseline (<=10 tickets per week).
success_criteria.validation_method: Compare weekly duplicate_charge_tickets from crm-tickets after change to baseline weeks 35-36.

rejected_framings.why: Evidence shows duplicate captures are gateway timeout retries lacking idempotency keys, not erroneous duplicate capture requests from checkout; PSP logs indicate second capture is a retry, not a new request.

proposal.root_problem: Disabled idempotency-key enforcement on the payment gateway causes gateway timeout retries to lack idempotency keys, leading to duplicate captures and customer double charges.
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice
causal_chain: Payment gateway idempotency-key enforcement is disabled (E-03).
A gateway timeout occurs during a capture attempt.
The shop's payment system automatically retries the capture without an idempotency key because enforcement is off.
The PSP processes the retry as a new capture (no deduplication) (E-01, E-02).
The order receives two captures, resulting in a duplicate charge.
The customer observes the double charge and files a support ticket (E-04, E-06).

assumptions.statement: Gateway timeout retries are automatically retried by the shop's payment system without manual intervention.
The PSP does not apply any other deduplication mechanism besides the idempotency key for capture retries.
The observed increase in duplicate charge tickets (E-04) is directly caused by duplicate captures and not by other billing issues.

unknowns.question: Whether re-enabling idempotency-key enforcement will immediately stop duplicate captures without causing other failures (e.g., increased latency or downtime).
unknowns.resolution_path: Run a canary test in a staging environment, then enable in production with close latency and error monitoring.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Continue manual refund processing and heightened ticket monitoring while the canary test runs.

unknowns.question: Whether other root causes (e.g., frontend double‑submit or race conditions) contribute to the observed duplicate charges.
unknowns.resolution_path: Analyze capture logs for duplicate requests that still contain an idempotency key; examine frontend click‑stream logs for duplicate submit events.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Maintain existing manual review of duplicate charge tickets and continue refunding confirmed duplicates.

unknowns.question: Whether the volume of duplicate charge tickets will drop to baseline after the fix, or if a backlog of existing disputes will persist.
unknowns.resolution_path: Track weekly duplicate‑charge ticket counts for four weeks after the change and compare to the pre‑incident baseline.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Keep the current SLA for ticket response and continue processing refunds as tickets arrive.

success_criteria.statement: Reduce duplicate charge rate to less than 0.1% (0.001) within two weeks of re‑enabling idempotency‑key enforcement.
success_criteria.validation_method: Calculate orders_with_2_captures / total_orders from the payments‑db (DA‑CHG) over a rolling two‑week window after the change.

rejected_framings.why: Contradicted by evidence: PSP logs show duplicate orders only when retries lack idempotency keys (E-01, E-02) and the PSP deduplicates retries when keys are present; no evidence of PSP‑side retry glitch.

While the hypothesis is marked SUPPORTED, the evidence points to missing idempotency on retries, not to the checkout sending duplicate capture requests; adopting this as the primary cause would misdirect effort.
